2464.text: Director Riddlevox put me in charge of the Union's shredder development program. Few months on the job and I'm already in hot water! I could use your help, $n!

2465.text: See, the Venture Company's new shredder is better than my latest, from the interchangeable hands to the control grips! My boss has given me a pretty strict deadline, but my boys and I couldn't come up with anything.$b$bNothing was working, so we decided to "borrow" one of their prototypes. I sent Wizzlecrank to the Sludge Fen to steal one, but he hasn't gotten back yet!

2529.text: Greetings, $c.  Are you here to learn of the hidden arts?
2529.text1: Greetings, $c.  Are you here to learn of the hidden arts?

2545.text1: It is not yet your time. I shall aid your journey back to the realm of the living... for a price.

2801.text: At last! I am finally free from this cell!$b$bThe Kirin Tor sent me from Dalaran to investigate Arugal's progress with the undead here in Silverpine Forest. Little did we know that the wizard had lost his grasp on sanity.$b$bI must report this mess at once! But before I leave, allow me to undo the magical lock on the courtyard door.$b$bYou defeated Rethilgore, perhaps you will survive what lies beyond....

2807.text: I once followed the ways of the Twilight's Hammer. Obsessed with reviving the Old Gods, I journeyed deep into this lair to try to draw power from the cursed beast, Aku'mai!$b$bAfter witnessing the sacrifice of countless innocents, I came to my senses.$b$bI was trapped but now I am free! But so far from my homeland of Khaz Modan!$b$bBrave adventurer, I offer you passage to a very special land in return for slaying Aku'mai. If you wish, I can port you to the city of Darnassus.

2825.text: As the wind on the plains, you are always welcome here.

3407.text: Where is it ye would like to go $g lad : lass;? For just a few coin my Gryphons can get ye there faster than even the swiftest horse.

3411.text: Speak quietly and with great care, the wrong word in these parts could get your throat cut. Now, what is it you need from me?
3411.text1: Speak quietly and with great care, the wrong word in these parts could get your throat cut. Now, what is it you need from me?

3742.text: In need of some alchemy supplies, are we?  Or do you have other business with me?

3792.text: Living out here in the desert is rough! I get so thirsty standing outside in this heat.

3813.text1: Hi there! I have a proposition for an adventure-seeker such as you, if you are up to the challenge!$B$BAlong with my invention, the Super Egg-O-Matic, I am hard at work aiding the druids with their campaign to save the hippogryphs. The birds are being affected by the evil effects of the Gordunni ogres inhabiting the ruins of Feralas, and their numbers are dwindling.$B$BI collect many different types of eggs.  Will you help and find some for me?

4139.text: Welcome to Blue Moon Odds and Ends, $c.  If you have any questions, please let me know.

4265.text1: I don't care to hear it, $n. Nope, no way are you going to be let into the Searing Gorge. Impossible. Not going to happen. How many times do I have to tell you - I can't let you in! Do you not speak common? Are you an orc in disguise? N-O. NO!$B$BIf I let you in, then I have to let everybody in. Pretty soon your close friends will want in, then their distant relatives, then their friends, and so on and so forth. The last time that happened... well, we won't talk about the last time it happened.

4498.text1: I am not here because of honor, $n. I am here because of one orc's pride.$B$BIf I had not rejected Belgrom's offers, then I'm sure I'd still be in Orgrimmar taking care of real business.$B$BHis debauchery is no secret to the female warriors in Durotar, but that certainly doesn't stop him from being his charming self.$B$BHe's lucky he didn't pursue his desire for me much longer though--he'd be short more than just the digits on his hands.

4511.text: I know, I know, I'm out here in the middle of nowhere!$B$BMy home is actually in Ratchet, but after crashing my zeppelin here, I thought I might as well start the research I came here to do!

4554.text: Hello there $glad:lass;... the name's Oglethorpe and I may be responsible for one of the amazing gnomish devices you might possess!  If it blew up, then it wasn't me; if it made you rich though, we can discuss royalties!$B$BOh, and if you're from Gnomeregan, you can just take two ninety degree angles, smash them together, and start marching.  I have nothing to say to you.

4555.text: Well, if it isn't $n!  It's good to see you again; I cannot express my gratitude enough at the help that you've given me and my invention work to date.$B$BWhat can I do for you today?

4556.text: I am Tinkmaster Overspark, and I am the chief architect for modern gnomish engineering principles in the world today.  It is my job to ensure that the power of invention continues to shine brightest from our arclight spanners than anywhere else!$B$BAlso, if you happen to know a good schematic for radiation elimination, we just so happen to be in the market for one right about now...

4565.text: Greetings, $c.  Though time and drink have dulled my outer senses, my inner eyes remain strong.

4581.text1: The arcane only corrupts those who are weak. Even if you do not follow the path of the warlock, you would do well to remember that.

4584.text: The arcane only corrupts those who are weak. Keep up on your training, or you may find a similar fate.
4584.text1: The arcane only corrupts those who are weak. Keep up on your training, or you may find a similar fate.

4617.text: Besides the Grunts outside, my brothers and I fought at the battle of Hyjal. Any who seek to steal from the bank must face us first.
4617.text1: Besides the Grunts outside, my brothers and I fought at the battle of Hyjal. Any who seek to steal from the bank must face us first.

4619.text: I guarantee this bank's security with my own blood, is that good enough for you?
4619.text1: I guarantee this bank's security with my own blood, is that good enough for you?

4621.text: Would you rather trust your goods with a goblin?
4621.text1: Would you rather trust your goods with a goblin?

4640.text: Welcome to Thelsamar, your home away from home in Loch Modan!$B$BThelsamar is a nice place, but it's not all beer and salted meat for those who answer the call to duty!  If you're willing to face danger in the name of the Alliance, then read the poster outside the Thelsamar branch of the Explorers' League.

4957.text: Welcome to Camp Mojache, brave $c.  How may I assist you this day?

4989.text: Hello, $n. If you'd like to learn a thing or two about cooking, please visit me at any time.

5274.text: Welcome to Tanaris, $n. How can I be of service to you today? You don't look like a blacksmith to me, but I know how looks can be deceiving.

5298.text: May the Light protect you this day.
5298.text1: May the Light protect you this day.

5472.text: Why you would want to leave these sunny shores and crystal blue waters I have no idea. It's like paradise down here. But don't tell my brother Zapetta that, he's bitter enough already about getting stuck up there in Tirisfal all day long. This Zeppelin here drops off at Orgrimmar so you shouldn't have to worry about having to listen to him whine. But if you are in Tirisfal anytime soon, heed my warning and don't get him started.

5520.text: Lady Sylvanas has ordered the investigation of some of the natural phenomena of Azeroth. She feels there is something great to be learned from its secretive past.$B$BI know not how she learned such things, but I trust her completely, so I will do my best.$B$BI am currently investigating slimes, oozes and such. The creatures all seem to be similar in make up, but greatly affected by their environment.$B$BI could use your help in gathering samples of the creatures..

5526.text: Greetings $g lad : lass;, if you're looking for the best deals you'll find outside of Ironforge itself, then you've come to the right place.

5533.text: ...pan fried, deep fried, and stir fried...

5627.text: Welcome to my shop, $c. What is it the Goodstitch brothers can do for you?

5729.text: Ye know more than I do, that's a certainty. Tell ye what though, go talk with me da'. He'll want ye ta prove yerself, but he is a fine teacher indeed. His name's Rotgath, and ye'll find him near the anvils workin steel for ol' Bengus.

5730.text: Well my friend, ye have more skill than I do. Why don't ye go find me old friend Rotgath Stonebeard. He stayed in Ironforge when I left to join Jaina's army. I'm sure he'll be able ta teach ye somethin, or at least know someone who can. If he's still around, I'm sure he'll be at The Great Forge.

5734.text: I don't admit this lightly, but you are a far better smith than I am. If you want to learn more than my meager teachings then I suggest you seek out a Dwarf named Therum Deepforge in Stormwind. You will find him in the Dwarven District.

5738.text: A far better blacksmith than I am, that's for sure. Though I'll deny it if you tell anyone I said that. You should go speak with Therum Deepforge. If anyone can teach you more, it's him.

5786.text: Aye, I would love ta teach ye a thing or two about smithing. Grab an apron and a hammer and let's see what we can accomplish shall we?

5922.text: Listen to the stories of an elder. $n. I have many to speak of...

6028.text1: Your errand must mean much, $c, to draw you so deep into the marsh...

6070.text: The Warchief has instructed me to study all kinds of weapons and armor. He has sent me here to the hub of both the tauren and orc cultures in the Barrens to meet as many travelers as possible, and to learn about the cultures of the Barrens.$B$BHe feels there's something to be learned from even the most pathetic of cultures... like the quilboar or centaur.

6644.text1: Hello young $g Master:Mistress;. I am Eva Sarkhoff and this is my husband, Lucien. It is a pleasure to make your acquaintance.

6646.text1: Certainly, $g sir:miss;. We were once servants of the house Barov: What is now known as the Scholomance.$B$BI was the head maid and Lucien was Master Barov's butler.$B$BWe had worked for the Barovs for decades, until...$B$B<Eva weeps.>

6648.text1: Oh it's just so horrible, $g sir:miss;. The house Barov was once full of life... full of splendor. The manor was the Barov's primary residence amidst their far reaching empire.$B$BLucien and I noticed that as the days progressed, the Barovs became depressed. Despondent. Paranoia and rage often overcame the master and missus. At night, we could hear the Barovs arguing in their chambers. From what we understood, their greed had 'broken the dam,' so to speak.

6650.text1: We suspect that in order to preserve their fortune and hold of the land - well past their lifespan - the Barovs made a deal with a powerful human mage named Kel'Thuzad.$B$B<Eva shudders.>$B$BFrom this deal sprang the school of necromancy: A place which bore the Cult of the Damned and would become their capital.$B$BAs each week passed, the house Barov became more and more decrepit...$B$BDark beings began to take residence in the various wings of the house. Upkeep became impossible... and disgusting.

6652.text1: And go where? It was all that we knew; all that we had known and all that we would ever know.$B$BEventually, we lost contact with the Barovs and ultimately, were separated from the household. We knew not what happened to the other servants, only that there were screams. Tortured screams.$B$BKnowing that we had nowhere to go, Lucien and I were forced to hide in our quarters. During the day, when the school was relatively quiet, Lucien would sneak out to scrounge up food and drink.

6654.text1: We did this for about six months and watched as the house went through horrifying changes. Foul monsters roamed through the manor at will. Dark cultists populated every inch with various paraphernalia relating to rituals and sacrifices. We knew that we could not hide much longer.$B$BAs expected, we were found and captured. They stripped us of all our clothes and laid us out inside a circle of blood. We sat there for days, naked and terrified.

6656.text1: Restraints? There are things in this world far more restraining than bars and shackles, young $g master:mistress;. The undead surrounded us, constantly tormenting us with horrifying acts of depravity.$B$BFinally, he came. He introduced himself as Doctor Theolen Krastinov. We came to know him as 'The Butcher.'

6658.text1: We finally understood what the screams were from. The Butcher exposed us to pain that we did not know existed. He used us in countless experiments, attempting to devise a plague.$B$BThe days turned to weeks. We would have died on the first day had it not been for that cruel bastard keeping us alive through magical means.

6660.text1: The Butcher would speak of 'the blood of innocents,' and his dark master, 'Kirtonos.' Of how he must appease his master.$B$BFinally, the beast was done with his experiments. We had been drained of all life. Our spirits shattered. The sweet embrace of death was upon us and we welcomed it with open arms. But in his infinite cruelty, the Butcher revived us from death's door.$B$BWe were to be kept alive and thrown to his ravenous ghouls. He laughed as he watched the fiends devour our flesh.

6662.text1: We feel nothing. Our souls remain here, in limbo. We are unable to leave until our remains are found and spirits laid to rest.

6869.text: Well met, friend.  I am Officer Garush, and I am a proud member of a world-wide organization known as the Argent Dawn.  Our cause is to fight swiftly and mercilessly against any element of evil that surfaces in Azeroth.  We are not a political body, nor do we ever wish to become one.  Our cause is singular, and to that end we call both the Horde and Alliance as friends - friends in the cause of stamping out evil!$B$BFor the Dawn, my $g brother : sister;!

7057.text: The skinners usually take all their hides into Ironforge to dry out.  Why don't you head there and see if you can find one to train ye?
7057.text1: The skinners usually take all their hides into Ironforge to dry out.  Why don't you head there and see if you can find one to train ye?

7197.text1: The plaguelands are an excellent place to strike against the Scourge!

7377.text: Slip a little coin into the boss's hand and look what it gets ya. I love my job. Though, if I could find a way to get that little firecracker Snurk reassigned to this port....well, I can't imagine it any better. But I'm betting that you aren't here about my business practices. You're looking for the Zeppelin to Undercity, am I right? Well that's great, because it docks right here behind me. Oh and hey, if you see Snurk, put a good word in for me, would ya?

7590.text: Hey, citizen!  You look like a stout one.  We guards are spread a little thin out here, and I could use your help...

7665.text: Where are you going?  Well if you're looking to get there quickly, then look no further!

7808.text1: Ah, what a beautiful day to blow something up!

7829.text: Hmm... well, I can't help you quite yet! You have to learn the basics first. Why don't you go see Sprite Jumpsprocket in Stormwind!

7834.text: You can learn from me in time... but not yet! Why don't you start out by talking to Sprite Jumpsprocket to my right here. You can check in with me after you've gotten your feet wet!

7918.text1: If I wasn't stuck here day in and day out, I would have attained the mastery required to train the likes of you! Unfortunately that's not the case. Go talk to Hgarth at the Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains.

7990.text: Sorry, but you've reached the limit of what I can teach. If you want to learn more, go see Telonis in the Craftsmen's Terrace of Darnassus. He's pretty talented, so I hear.

7995.text: If you are here for further training, you have overestimated my abilities. Have a word with Telonis over there; he can help you.

8045.text: Do not try to force your will upon the leather. Rather, let its natural tendencies dictate what form and function it will take. This is not a battle to be won. Work with the leather, not against it.

8047.text1: Even my talents have a limit, and you have reached it. Congratulations, $n. Your next stop should be Camp Mojache in Feralas. The tauren Hahrana Ironhide lives there; she is renowned for her skill.

8057.text1: We cannot afford to give an inch in this war. Day and night, I create new armor, and I patch whatever can be salvaged from the old. I have no time for other tasks. Would you take care of something for me?

8072.text: I know a few things, but I'm no expert. Lucky for you, Magar is. He's standing near the back of the shop. See if he can help you, but be careful not to rile him. He can be irritable.

8095.text: How may I be of service?

8096.text: Greetings, and welcome.  I am not very good at smiling, but trust me; I am happy to serve you.

8098.text1: The Hippogryph is a noble beast, proud and swift.  They are an honor to train, and can quickly take their rider a great distance.

8099.text: To maintain our link to the mainland, we have hippogryphs constantly flying between Rut'theran Village and Darkshore.

8104.text: Fastest gryphons this side of Aerie Peak. Want to take a ride?

8111.text: My wind riders are trained to fly quickly through the hot Barrens air.

8113.text: Delivering these barrels to the excavation site is hard work, but there are so many depending on us to get the blast powder there.$B$BWe must do what we can against the Dark Irons!

8116.text: When mounted on the back of a wind rider, one sees that its reputation for strength and speed is well earned.

8122.text: You haven't lived until you've looked down on the world from the back of a wind rider.

8151.text: About time you showed me some results! Now I'll show you results!

8156.text: Well well, not too bad. Maybe I CAN show you a few things...

8209.text: Mark my words!  You won't find faster gryphons anywhere in the Eastern Kingdoms than the ones right here in Thelsamar!

8217.text: The Wildhammer dwarves might have fast steeds, but can those Aerie Peak gryphons stand the heat of The Great Forge?  I think not!

8220.text: The best miner has a firm grip on $ghis:her; pick, a stout heart in $ghis:her; chest, and thick, black dust in $ghis:her; hair.

8260.text: Through rigorous retraining I have had to break many students of all they had previously learned so that I might teach them anew.  The service I offer becomes increasingly difficult to perform each time it is done.  It is for that reason that it becomes increasingly expensive with each retraining.  Do you desire that I break you of the talents you have learned?
8260.text1: Through rigorous retraining I have had to break many students of all they had previously learned so that I might teach them anew. Do you desire that I break you of the talents you have learned?

8264.text: Look at the wisdom and knowledge of the beast, and you will see yourself. Observe as the owl does, learn cleverness from the sabercat, embody the mighty spirit of the wolf.
8264.text1: Look at the wisdom and knowledge of the beast, and you will see yourself. Observe as the owl does, learn cleverness from the sabercat, embody the mighty spirit of the wolf.

8325.text: I see some interesting characters come and go here at the port. Watch yourself, $n. It's never clear who to trust, what with all of the shady activity that goes on here...

8334.text: Fish so delicious. You come learn fish? Eat fish? Mmmmm...

8344.text: We may have been suffering a drought but there's no shortage of meat! Care to browse my goods?

8348.text: I keep 'em fed, kid. Yep, Daryl Riknussun, at yer service.

8368.text1: Are you a student of the medical sciences?

8402.text: Want to make your demons more powerful?  It'll cost you, but you've come to the right place.
8402.text1: Want to make your demons more powerful?  It'll cost you, but you've come to the right place.

8881.text: Ye want to be trained in the use of a weapon, do ye?  Well don't stand there slack-jawed, speak up $gladdie : lassie;!

8883.text1: Well hi there!  Are you here to learn the proper technique of a new weapon?

8919.text1: My sisters and I have come down from the Stonetalon Mountains to put to rest a tragedy from ages past. Unfortunately, we are not powerful enough to accomplish our goals on our own and now seek mortals such as yourself to aid us.$B$BIf you are powerful enough, then we have much to discuss, $c. If you are not, then, for your safety, I will leave the details of my mission out of our conversation.

8924.text: I need no home to know I still have a place in this world, $c. The tribes will see... all of them. They fight amongst one another, and for what? Scraps left over by vultures... lands infested by the Legion... bah!$B$BThe centaur should be proud of their heritage--it is just as noble as any Night elf's or orc's--it is time we started acting like it!

8925.text: At last, I am free of the corruption that once bound me to this place...

8930.text: My scepter... After so many years... You have recovered it! You shall truly be the savior of this place...$B$BPlease listen to me carefully, $n. The head and the rod of the scepter may only be reunited into one at the Stone of Maraudon.

9017.text: Master Nesingwary has a big hunt ahead of him.  I find helping him prepare for a day in the jungle is much more relaxing than helping him ready for combat.  Although I do miss some of those glorious moments on the battlefield.

9029.text1: Hi there. No, Marvon sure isn't here, and he won't be back for quite some time. Actually, I am getting a little worried about him...$B$BI hope he gets back soon. A large chest arrived for him and it's too heavy for me to lug it inside here! I had to leave it out by the door...

9032.text1: This place... it's cursed.$B$BI barely managed to escape, and I cannot bear to go down through the tunnels again.$B$BMy brother, and sisters though... They were not as fortunate. Trapped inside, they are feverish with the corrupted haze that flows from the evil garden growing there.$B$BPlease, you must help.

9350.text: Do you want to play a game, stinky?

9473.text: What you must understand is that being able to index 10,000 years of existence has given me a rather unique perspective on life. Your present day trials and tribulations are meaningless.

9557.text: I can teach you fishing skills.
9557.text1: I can teach you fishing skills.

9659.text1: There are costs with war, $c... ones often overlooked.  Those costs are the orphans - children who have lost their parents to the far-too-numerous conflicts that rage across Azeroth.  Those children who have no one else to turn to often come here to live until they are old enough to fend for themselves.$B$BOne week out of the year during the Spring, the Alliance takes time to give something back to these innocents.  This time is called Children's Week.

9685.text: Cooking is a life long pursuit and I see we share the same passion!
9685.text1: Cooking is a life long pursuit and I see we share the same passion!

9688.text: I can teach you how to cook!
9688.text1: I can teach you how to cook!

9701.text: I can train you in First Aid techniques.
9701.text1: I can train you in First Aid techniques.

9877.text: Are you interested in exploring one of these dungeons?

292961.text:
Professions are divided between two main categories: primary and secondary.

You are limited to a maximum of two primary professions at a time. You can abandon your skill in a primary profession at any time; however, the wealth of knowledge you gathered for it will be lost. If you choose to return to your original profession, you will need to train from the basics and seek out recipes you previously acquired to refamiliarize yourself with them.

Secondary professions do not have such a limit. These skills tend to err towards self-sufficiency with your basic survival needs. You are free to train any or all of these, but may find fewer opportunities to turn a profit.

300037.text: H-Hello. You'll have to excuse me, I'm used to your kind running from me.

300039.text:
That is... a very good question. I have a hard time remembering things, but I do remember something... "Engineer", perhaps? I think that's what, or who, I was.

Other than that, all I can seem to remember is soaring through the sky, then seeing a flash of lightning before things got very bumpy. Then... a crash.

It's been... a long time though. A very long time.

300042.text:
Oh, these things? I built them. My little friends helped me. I'm not very good at remembering things, but, um, I do know that at one point I used to build a lot of things. Big things! But then, like I said... I was here. The things I build aren't so big and impressive anymore. Still makes me h-happy, heh.

B-but... If you want, I can show you how to build things too!

300626.text1: Greetings, $c. Do you come seeking the blessings of the Windlord?

300661.text: Ho there, traveler! New to town? Well, once you get settled in, come see me if you'd like some work. I've been working overtime preparing for the Festival of Winds and I'll take all the help I can get keeping the larders full!

300662.text: If you need training as a cook, I have a few tips and tricks I could pass on! Ho ho! Throw on an apron and let's get started!

300665.text1: I'm in charge of Shen'dar Village operations, and there's a lot of things to keep track of around here. Between bandits, cultists, and other random incidents that pop up, keeping this village afloat is a lot of work.

300678.text1: <Constable Aonda wears an intense look on her face, clearly deep in thought.>

300698.text: I can teach you to craft fine leather armor, if you have the aptitude.

300702.text1:
The clothcraft of the Shen'dorei is a harmonious imitation of the flowing, carefree currents of the winds. While the spirits have left us, and I know not when I may see them dance once more... I find great comfort in my art, if only as a distraction.

I can teach you to work the cloth as well, if you'd like to learn?

Our kind are rare these days, but there are those who still dream in emerald amongst the shen'dorei.

Keep your eyes open in the forest. The right light can reveal that which is hidden, protected by the north wind.

301009.text:
Greetings, young $c. Welcome to the hall of the Tradesman's Guild. Resources are tight on Zephras right now, but you should be able to find a variety of materials and wares here to keep you in top adventuring form.

Please let me know if you have any questions.
301009.text1:
Greetings, young $c. Welcome to the hall of the Tradesman's Guild. Resources are tight on Zephras right now, but you should be able to find a variety of materials and wares here to keep you in top adventuring form.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

301019.text: Come, young one, sit with me.

301020.text: The pylons that keep our island home anchored to the elemental plane of Skywall are failing. Zephras Isle--our home--is in grave danger.

301021.text: The Al'Aketh cult continues to escalate their violence, and the Windshapers stubbornly refuse to recognize the inaction that brought us here.

301022.text: The High Order are the custodians of the highborne ways, and we will master the magic holding this island in place and bend it to our will.

301023.text: The future is uncertain, but there is opportunity in this. We will rediscover the self-reliance that drove us before we came to this place.

301024.text: It was a critical mistake that our people left their fates in the hands of fickle elemental spirits. It's up to us now to remedy that error.

301032.text: Where to begin? Our home is failing. The wards have fallen and the three provinces have begun to drift apart. There was a time not long ago when the spires of Shen'dramar were visible from the western watchtower. No longer. Day by day the wind pylons that anchor our home to this plane weaken...

301033.text:
Why is this happening? Put simply, the spirits of the wind just... vanished. 

The petty sprites and lesser elementals you've likely encountered out there are a pale imitation of the true spirits of wind. Non-sentient, aimless, and a far cry from the kindly spirits we lived in harmony alongside for thousands of years.

301034.text: Many disagree on this point. The Windshapers would have you believe that joining hands and merely hoping for the spirits' return will be sufficient. Their order's power has waned, however, and their path relies on putting us back on the cycle of dependence that got us to this point. The High Order, on the other hand... we believe in a more direct approach.

301035.text:
The Cult? They are zealots and killers. They believe that we are being punished for some unspecific sin. The reality is that those that lead them are opportunists left over from a dubious order of so-called "Priests" of Al'Akir, the Windlord.

They now find themselves in a position to weaponize the fear of our people to consolidate their own power... and they have been quick to do so.

301036.text:
Even the Windshapers would tell you that the spirits never spoke highly of any supreme being amongst them. They acknowledged the existence of a being named Al'Akir, but they avoided invoking his name, almost as if they feared him.

Even if this Al'Akir is an all-powerful "Windlord" or ruler of the wind elementals, relying upon elementals is what got us into this mess. We must now see ourselves out of it.

301037.text:
You must remember that while this realm has been our home for millennia, we will always be somewhat alien to this place. We are not in the terrestrial world that birthed our people. We are in the realm of Skywall, the elemental plane of air.

We arrived here as the guests of spirits with whom we found kinship in ages past. Now that we shen'dorei find ourselves bereft of their presence--and potentially--their protection, there's no telling how the other denizens of this plane may perceive us.

301038.text: Alas, I have prattled on long enough. Should you find yourself in the port of Valanaar, seek out Elaadrin Evengale. Elaadrin was once my student, but now he serves as the Chief Magister of the High Order. He is headstrong and capable, and it's now up to him and young Skyborne such as yourself to carry the hopes for our people forward.

301040.text1: If you are looking for more work, I'm sure there are some folks in town that are also looking for help with one task or another. Just ask around, you are bound to find something.

301044.text:
Hello there, young $c. I am Rathiril Sunlance and I am an elder Magister of the High Order here on Zephras Isle. It's always good to see bright-eyed young shen'dorei, ready to do their duty in service to their homeland.

Don't let this dusty old mage hold you up, however. No doubt you've got many adventures to see to. Feel free to stop by later if you'd like to speak more.

301355.text: My wife and I run the stormapple orchard in the lowlands, just to the west of Valanaar.

301356.text: Some years ago our farm was attacked by bandits. They took everything we had and left me bruised and bloody. The next season around the same time, they returned.

301357.text: They took most of our harvest again, but this time the bandit leader--Ferauu "the Bludgeon" as he's known--told us that every season they'd return and take twice as much as the previous year.

301358.text: We tried to petition the peacekeepers to come and help drive the bandits off, but they are stretched too thin just dealing with the cult and couldn't spare anyone.

301359.text: This year our yield is light and we can't hope to give them what they expect. The best case is that they simply kill us quickly. It's more likely they take everything we have and leave us to starve.

301362.text: I came to town to hire fighters to drive them off. I found one warrior who agreed to help, but he robbed me as soon as we were out of town and nearly beat me to death.

301364.text: At this point I'm too injured to leave this bed. I'm begging you, stranger. Travel to my orchard. Tell Aamelia what happened and help her survive this somehow. Please, stranger... help us.

301399.text1: The Windfield Orchard has seen better days...

301445.text: Aamelia, my dear. Where's Alvarion? Too afraid to come and face Ferauu, so he sent you?

301446.text1: Alvarion? Oh he's still in the hills with the peacekeepers, clearing out the rest of your lackeys. I'm sure they'll be along any minute and would love to see you.

301447.text: HA! A poor bluff! Ferauu has eyes and ears everywhere. I know that it's just you and this scrawny stranger here. You've had your fun putting down a few of my weaker recruits, but The Bludgeon is here now and the party is over. Time to pay up, with interest.

301448.text1: I'm done talking. Stranger, thanks for everything...

301449.text1: Aamelia raises her pitchfork, ready to fight.

301450.text1: Huh. Well that was... unexpected. I guess we know what that big lug's purpose is now. Let's head back to the house, stranger.

301455.text: <The man lying before you shifts uncomfortably. He's recovering from some very nasty wounds.>

301456.text: It's always great to see you, $n.

301458.text:
Hmm, what an odd question? Not much, I suppose. My mother used to use it as a powder for babies to prevent diaper rash, but past that, I don't know of any other good use for it.

Why do you ask?

301472.text: If you've spoken with Rathiril and he sent you to see me, you are no doubt aware of the peril we find ourselves in.

301473.text: The High Order seeks to find a pragmatic and enlightened solution to our current crisis.

301474.text: One that does not rely upon divine intervention from external forces. We seek to master our own destiny for the first time since we've arrived in Skywall.

301475.text: Since we left our homes in Kalimdor, the world has grown. They call it "Azeroth" now and it's a massive, vibrant world.

301476.text: Recently we discovered a way to use our magic to carve a "keyhole" of sorts to peer through the planes to learn much of Azeroth.

301478.text: When we peered through that keyhole, someone else peered back--members of a magical order much like our own, called the Kirin Tor. We have learned much from them.

301480.text: The elementals who brought us here are gone. Any feats they used to maintain our homes can be replicated with highborne magic, but our powers have grown weak in Skywall.

301481.text: Some among us must leave this plane of existence. We must travel to Azeroth to rediscover what we've lost, and bring that knowledge back as a tool to save our home.

301482.text: The Kirin Tor have graciously agreed to receive us as their guests, and we will need their help if we are to succeed.

301483.text: We will need explorers and adventurers of all kinds. Think on this, and when the time comes, I hope you will consider joining us. Until then, good fortune to you.

301834.text: There won't be an explosion. The detonator I gave you was designed to fail.

301836.text: SI:7 will take things from here. The forge and warship you liberated from the Defias have strategic value and we are taking control of them.

301837.text1: You don't understand. That forge is poisoning the farms of Westfall! If it isn't destroyed, nothing will grow here for generations. You're risking a major famine!

301838.text: Thank you for your concern, elf, but this is now a Stormwind internal matter. Your help is no longer needed at this time.

301844.text: My... head... ohh it hurts! What... who are you? Why... are you carrying me?

301845.text: Stranger... please... put me down... on the bedroll by that tree there...

On behalf of Darnassus I would like to offer my aid in replenishing this land. Will you assist me?

301874.text: It is encouraging to know that Elaadrin and his mages are finally with us. With both the High Order and the Windshapers working with us against the greater threat, we stand a much better chance to thwart the Al'Aketh and whatever they have planned for Valanaar.

301876.text: Oh, and for you in particular, $c. I heard of the altercation you had at the standing stones with the Windshapers...

301877.text: There may yet be a reckoning for that. In the meantime, I hope that both the Windshapers and the High Order can agree that the Al'Aketh are the greater threat to Zephras and set all else aside.

302063.text1: With the cult running roughshod over most of the island with impunity, Lorthuna undoubtedly thinks we are on the back foot. We can use that overconfidence against her.

302064.text1: I believe that with a proper distraction at the shrine, a small force of Peacekeepers, Windshapers, and High Order should be able to push up a flank and break into the inner sanctum. From there, we take out the High Priestess herself and cut the head off the snake.

302065.text1: Go and speak with the leaders of the Windshapers and the High Order, respectively. They don't get along, but I think they can recognize that the bigger threat is the Al'Aketh. Get them to agree to the plan and then return here.

302070.text1:
<Ayessa Dawnsinger eyes you with barely-contained fury.> 

You are either very bold, or very stupid to so brazenly step foot into our domain after spilling Windshaper blood. We are slow to forgive, and we never forget. 

You should remove yourself from here at once. If we weren't in the center of Zephras, you would already be dead.

302073.text1:
Hmm, I see. Very well then, $c. The Windshapers will provide aid. Please inform Valennia that she can count on us for this fight.

<Ayessa lowers her voice dangerously.> 

Do not mistake our cooperation for any sort of forgiveness. You owe the Windshapers blood, and someday we will collect.

302079.text: Greetings, I am Elaadrin Evengale, the current Supreme Magister of the High Order. How can I help you?

302085.text:
The Windshapers are almost wholly to blame for everything that has happened. Their refusal to change has damaged our ability to save ourselves from our current peril. They speak in absolutes and treat assumptions and superstitious hope as fact.

Do you know who else deals only in absolutes? The Al'Aketh. 

I for one do not intend to let blind adherence to dangerous beliefs doom our people. If it weren't for the threat of the cult, I'd march our mages over to the other side of Valanaar and wipe the Windshapers out.

302087.text:
I see. This seems dangerous in the extreme, but the situation seems to demand that risks be taken.

Very well, the High Order will provide aid. Please inform Valennia that she can count on us for this fight.

302093.text:
The Peacekeepers can't hope to muster the numbers needed for an outright assault on the shrine. Without the Windshapers and the High Order bolstering our numbers, we stand no chance. They both pledged their aid when we need it. Now is the time.

Unfortunately, some recent events have led to outright bloodshed between the two factions, and tensions are high.

How do you feel about a bit of diplomacy?

The Peacekeepers can't hope to muster the numbers needed for an outright assault on the shrine. Without the Windshapers and the High Order bolstering our numbers, we stand no chance. They both pledged their aid when we need it. Now is the time.

302159.text1: <Valennia is severely wounded and is barely holding on to consciousness.>

302160.text1:
Most of the cultists at the Sanctum of Storms seem to have come out to respond to our attack. I never would have expected this to go so well. This was almost too easy...

I think that the Windshapers and High Order have made their push. Valennia should be with them. You should head inside and find her. We'll stay here and keep watch while Valennia and the others finish what they came here to do.

302214.text:
The full story requires time that I suspect you do not have, so I will attempt to be brief.

Perhaps the simplest way I can put it: these crystals are anchors. They can be used to permanently--well, so long as the crystals hold I suppose--bind something, someone, or even somewhere onto our plane of Azeroth. Prince Tortheldrin ordered the creation of similar pylons when he chose to bind the demon Immol'thar. Some of the Shen'dralar protested this decision and proposed a compelling alternative, but ultimately the prince was uninterested in debate and eager to silence dissent.

I had an opportunity to study their design before it became too unsafe for me to stay within the city's walls and I fled back to Shen'dralas.

302215.text:
The proposed alternative to demonic entanglement was at odds with what Tortheldrin had already set in motion. Given that he was working with power that tends to cloud one's judgment, it's no surprise that his first instinct was to lash out.

Most everyone who pushed back against his plans to summon and bind a demon were slain that day. Some escaped, including some of my own kin that stood in opposition to the prince, but I have yet to meet other survivors of that schism even after all these thousands of years.

302216.text:
I suspected that my fallen brethren would be too stubborn to pass on from Eldre'Thalas completely, and assumed they would either haunt those halls for eternity or venture north to this place here to live out whatever afterlives they sought out for themselves. I painstakingly created these crystals to anchor their spirits more closely with Azeroth, allowing them to experience the world almost as though they were alive.

Indeed, it worked then. And I suspect it is working again now. I think they will be appreciative of you restoring some of their corporeality.

You should go meet them.

302443.text: We came as soon as we were told what was happening. The High Order is here to serve Zephras.

302444.text1: ...and the Windshapers. We are ready to support an assault on the Shrine, Valennia.

302445.text1: You have my thanks. Being truthful, however, this is going to be a dangerous gambit and we may not succeed. It's important you understand that this might be a one-way ride.

302446.text1: We understand. As it happens Elaadrin and I spoke. We made arrangements to send for... outside aid. It's unclear if they will be able to arrive in time to help, or if they will even arrive at all...

302447.text1: Outside... of Zephras? From the other provinces? We haven't had contact with the other islands for years...?

302448.text: It's... coming from a little further away than that. We'll explain on the way.

302449.text1: Very well then. Time is not with us so we should make ourselves ready. Thank you all for your aid. Zephras is in your debt.

302631.text1: Aonda is a good woman, and a true servant of Zephras Isle. It is my hope that you can quickly earn her trust and help her to keep Shen'dar Village safe. May the winds guide you, $n.

302649.text1: Go with the blessings of Al'Akir. But be warned; those that approach the Windlord's faithful under false pretense will quickly face His wrath.

302705.text: I tell you lot, that forest is haunted! I SAW *hic* WHAT I SAW!

302706.text: If you don't believe me, go and see for yourself! Terrible windblown wraiths *hic*... forest spirits that will gnaw your ankles!

302707.text: There's even a terrible forest wraith! Dressed all in black and... evil looking! I tell you, it's a cursed place! *hic*

302809.text: The followers of the old Highborne ways have never been more hungry to gain knowledge and reclaim what we've lost. If you would seek to wield the power of the arcane and have the aptitude, I can help you take your next steps.

The hunters and rangers of Zephras have never been more needed. The winds grow ever harsher, and the magic that sustains our island is fading. The wilds have never been more wild, and people like me are needed to keep our people safe.

If you have the proper aptitude as a hunter, I can give you the tools to survive the wilds.

If you have the proper aptitude as a hunter, I can give you the tools to survive the wilds.

302854.text: The Alliance has many stakes in Desolace, and our hold here is unstable.$B$BWill you help us?

303234.text1:
The whole of this valley was once a garden of Eldre'Thalas, but that blighted land ahead of us was the highlight of it all. Nearly everyone contributed to its arrangement and growth. When tensions were high, often many of us would take a stroll to clear our minds.

Had it withered purely from neglect, I suspect it would look no different than the rest of Shen'dralas.

303328.text:
I tended to these gardens long ago. I plucked the weeds. Trimmed the shrubbery. Planted the flowers. Alongside an elven woman, and her enchanted amulet.

Time passed. My bark aged. Weeds retaliated. Bushes wilted. Flowers withered. My branches were stiff and my movement slow, yet the elf and her people still smiled. What I could no longer do, they did in my stead.

But they stopped suddenly. This valley grew quiet. Dark. But all was well, with the elven woman's gift. Then, it was taken.

I was left with no choice. I set myself aflame. To burn it all down. So the restless weeds would not spread further.

I have died, but I still burn. The weeds still grow. I have failed.

303584.text: Oh, that's okay. I-I'll be here if you want to learn some other time. T-Thank you for talking to me!

303598.text1: Oh, and a word of warning before you head up to Shadowgale Forest. It's incredibly dangerous up there. Some even say it's haunted. Make sure you are prepared and well-equipped if you plan to make the trek.

303612.text: Welcome to the Calmbreeze Inn, traveler. Would you like some refreshment?
303612.text1: Welcome to the Calmbreeze Inn, traveler. Would you like some refreshment?

303927.text1: A visitor to Shen'dralas? To what do we owe the pleasure?

304010.text: What do you need of me, child of Zephras?

304012.text1: What may I do for you, fellow windshaper?

304014.text: Greetings to you, fellow High Order initiate.

304291.text:
Lorthuna is performing some sort of ritual up there. She may be trying to bring down the wards!

The help we sent for has not yet arrived, but we'll just have to manage with what we have. When you are ready, let me know and we'll go confront her.

304299.text1: Lorthuna! Stop this madness. You don't know what bringing down the wards protecting Zephras will do. You could doom us all!

304303.text1: Ayessa... my former sister. How far you've fallen, keeping company with this High Order filth.

304304.text: I'll make this easy for you, witch. Stop what you are doing now and I will make your death swift. This is the last and best offer you will get from the High Order.

304307.text1: Bring the wards down? The wards have been down for days, fools. No, I am merely lighting a beacon... for the true servants of Al'Akir to follow.

304433.text1: Ahh... yes! The call has been answered. Meet your end with joy!

304441.text: Who dares call the Lord of the East Wind?

304443.text: So the rumors were true. My wayward brothers did well to conceal this place from the gaze of Al'Akir.

304445.text1: Yes! Yes! It is by my will that the way to Zephras is open to you! Bring me before your Windlord so that he may know who was the herald of his glory!

304447.text: You dare to command me, mortal? No, I think not. Begone, insignificant elf!

304448.text1: No! Never, I would never dare!

304449.text: Well, you certainly never will again, insect. Hah!

304452.text: Enjoy your remaining time as "guests" in my lord's realm until his judgement inevitably arrives. You'll know not when, but it is coming.

304454.text: Now that this wondrous realm is no longer hidden from us, you are going to enjoy getting to know the TRUE children of Skywall...

304558.text: Oh, enough of that crazy talk, swimmers. You are going to scare off the few customers we have with your drunken ghost stories!
304558.text1: Oh, enough of that crazy talk, swimmers. You are going to scare off the few customers we have with your drunken ghost stories!

304612.text: Welcome to Shen'dar Village, some of the best fishing this side of the mountain range. If you are looking to catch fish, I can teach you, for a price.

304927.text: Ah, nothing beats the smell of fresh air with a hint of sweet sap.

305008.text: <A solitary bandit sits on the edge of the precipice, clearly deep in thought. If he notices you, he doesn't seem interested in attacking you.>
305008.text1: <A solitary bandit sits on the edge of the precipice, clearly deep in thought. If he notices you, he doesn't seem interested in attacking you.>

305012.text: Just thinking. It's scary out here these days, you know? Any minute this section of the island could drop out from under me and I'd go tumbling... somewhere? Tell me, do you even know what happens to skyborne who fall off the island?
305012.text1: Just thinking. It's scary out here these days, you know? Any minute this section of the island could drop out from under me and I'd go tumbling... somewhere? Tell me, do you even know what happens to skyborne who fall off the island?

305015.text:
No one does. Because the only people who've done it have never come back. When the skycutters used to run between Valanaar and New Eldranaar or Shen'dramar, sometimes an accident or other misfortune would cause someone to go overboard. When it happened, they wouldn't even slow the ship down. No point.

For all we know, anyone who fell off is still out there... tumbling endlessly forever.

305017.text: Look around you. There's so much beauty here. The wind on your face, the blue skies overhead. It's so bright and alive, but yes, it's also quite dark. It feels like a prison. A prison where the guards have all left the prisoners in their cells to fend for themselves.

305019.text: Anyway, I should probably get back to work. Speaking of, do you have any food or valuables that I could lift off of you? Maybe some windstones? Could always use more windstones?
305019.text1: Anyway, I should probably get back to work. Speaking of, do you have any food or valuables that I could lift off of you? Maybe some windstones? Could always use more windstones?

305021.text: You don't look like much, but something tells me you are right. I think I'll just sit here a bit longer. Thanks for the chat, stranger.
305021.text1: You don't look like much, but something tells me you are right. I think I'll just sit here a bit longer. Thanks for the chat, stranger.

305106.text: Sorry that we are late, Ayessa.

305107.text: It took a bit of work to convince Archmage Rhonin to help me open that transplanar portal...

305108.text: Ansirem! This isn't how I expected our first meeting to go, but I'm glad you made it!

305109.text1: Nor is this how I envisioned our first meeting, Muln.

305110.text: Well if this isn't an inspirational sight. The little elves seem to have friends in... low places.

305111.text: We have no quarrel with you, Lord of the East Wind. Leave us in peace.

305112.text: Very well, mortals. For now enjoy your respite. I simply cannot wait to tell the Windlord about all that has transpired here. You will be seeing me again... very soon.

305131.text1: Empty threats, Elaadrin. Regardless of what happens to me now, my great work is done. Consider yourself lucky to be here at the eye of the storm, to witness the fruits of our labor.

305132.text: Wait... what is this place? How could such a place exist in the Windlord's realm?

305133.text: I think it's time for us to be leaving this place. I will open a portal to Valanaar.

305134.text1: Muln Earthfury of the Earthen Ring--the Windshapers would be happy to accept you as our guest.

305135.text: Yes, and you, Archmage Runeweaver. The High Order is eager to learn more of the Kirin Tor.

305160.text: Adventurer! The wind bridge leading to the other spire is unstable. You may need to wait here with me until it returns.
305160.text1: Adventurer! The wind bridge leading to the other spire is unstable. You may need to wait here with me until it returns.

305765.text: The skycutters and ferries haven't run in years at this point. For all we know, there are no other islands left for us to get imports from. Still though, I'm here... just in case.

305849.text: High Priestess, we are ready to carry out your will. I will move on the western watchtower, and Commander Cyclas will lead the attack on Shen'dar Village. Both will be ours by tomorrow.

305850.text1: The great work is nearly complete, Skypriest Aanders. Your success here is vital.

305851.text: Of course, High Priestess. We are the instruments of your will. I only wish you could be here to witness our triumph firsthand.
305851.text1: Of course, High Priestess. We are the instruments of your will. I only wish you could be here to witness our triumph firsthand.

305852.text1: I am needed elsewhere for now and this represents but one piece on the gameboard. Do not fail me, Aanders.

305854.text: Do you seek the blessings of the Windlord?
305854.text1: Do you seek the blessings of the Windlord?

306261.text1: It appears the winds have brought you my way! I am happy to train you in the ways of cooking if you have the inclination to learn.

306266.text1:
Cooking on Zephras may seem difficult to the untrained eye, but I enjoy the creation of every dish. Even though our dwindling home is lacking many of our traditional kaldorei ingredients, it has been fun to create new variations of the recipes of our ancestors.

I hope that no matter where the winds take you, these recipes remind you of home.

306273.text: I hope that your interruption is for a good cause. I was in the middle of some important work.
306273.text1: I hope that your interruption is for a good cause. I was in the middle of some important work.

306274.text: Gales greetings, friend. Is there something I can help you with?
306274.text1: Gales greetings, friend. Is there something I can help you with?

306276.text: Ah, hello. You look as though you have a question for me.

306278.text: Winds tidings. What can I help you with?

307135.text:
Welcome to Shen'dralas, or what remains of it.

I hope you can appreciate the majesty of this place, even if it is a haunted shell of its former self.

307136.text:
This was once a part of Eldre'Thalas - the ancient city of my people that lies just over the southern mountains. Dire Maul, I believe it is commonly called these days. Perhaps you have heard of it.

Over time, the elements have worn away at our marvelous structures and smothered our gardens. I yearn to return to the halls of Eldre'Thalas, but I am still haunted by memories of the past.

For now, I am content merely watching over these lands and reminiscing over what once was.

307408.text: Ye've come further than many, $n. Respect the elements around ye and ye shall fare far greater than most.
307408.text1: Ye've come further than many, $n. Respect the elements around ye and ye shall fare far greater than most.

307841.text:
Ah, it's been some time since we've had adventurers roam these halls. Welcome to Farholde Keep. Enjoy these comforts while you can. I'm sure you've seen the conditions we're forced to keep.

It seems every day we lose more of our home to the ever-growing infestation of Horde mongrels and Light-forsaken Twilight's Hammer cultists. With those cowards in Stormwind hiding behind their walls, we are forced to bring order to these beasts ourselves.

Perhaps you'd like to put some of those $c talents to use?

307855.text1: Greetings, $c. As advisor to Demar, I would be happy to answer any questions you have about Farholde Keep.

307912.text: Watch yourself, $c. The Windshapers will not tolerate hostility from the High Order.
307912.text1: Watch yourself, $c. The Windshapers will not tolerate hostility from the High Order.

308645.text1:
Ah, a worldly explorer!

Can you smell that fresh, ocean air? Just don't inhale too deeply. Sometimes it smells a bit fishy.

309436.text: Do you require training in the ways of the light?
309436.text1: Do you require training in the ways of the light?

309474.text:
<Before you lies a skyborne; his body is mangled and bruised but still recognizable. It is clear he met a gruesome end while attempting to flee.

It appears that all of his belongings are still on his body, and a half-filled crate nearby lies spilled on the ground.>

309776.text1:
Hey hey hey! Watch where you're trackin' your shoes.

Tryin' to run a classy establishment here!

309779.text:
No fights goin' on today, pal. The Horde and the Alliance are too busy killin' each other out in the fields when there's perfectly good coin to be made doin' that in my arena! Go figure.

Come back when I get this place up and runnin'.

309852.text: The ingots are for display only!

309855.text: Hello there! I've got the finest leathers this side of Stormwind. Interested?

309858.text: You won't find better equipment anywhere else!

309859.text: Oh! Greetings, friend. Feel free to browse my wares.

309862.text:
<Jim'bek locks eyes with you as he takes a deep puff from his hookah.>

'Ello, mon. Need a rug? A blanket? Or just some cloth for your next project? I got you.

310295.text: I'm not a club, you imbecile!

310771.text: They are going to see somethin' really scary!

310796.text: Ye think you can stop the greatest heist in history?

310797.text: I nearly... got away... with it.

310819.text: Even in death... I will persist.

311268.text: In the northwestern mountain range of Azshara, due north of the Ruins of Eldarath, there is an old passage that leads into the heart of Blackmaw Hold.
311268.text1: In the northwestern mountain range of Azshara, due north of the Ruins of Eldarath, there is an old passage that leads into the heart of Blackmaw Hold.

311269.text: The Blackmaw tribe holds this stronghold as their home. If you are journeying into northern Azshara, be on your guard, as the Blackmaw tribe is wary of all strangers as many of their kin have fallen to corruption and the animosity that we show them is returned by the Blackmaw as a measure of safety.

312713.text: It can get boring up here, you know. I can only annoy that stuffy wretch Halaan so much before even that gets old.

312724.text: You there! Be careful! Your sacred shen'dorei gifts are not to be used for amusement!

312958.text:
What the hell do you want? Can't you see I'm busy here?

Why don't you make yourself useful and have Zizplink pour me another drink. Mine's running dry.

313248.text: Go on and have a seat near the fire and we can get started.

313249.text: All you need to start a camp of your own is a basic campfire. Cooks can generally teach you how to make one of those.

313250.text: Once your campfire is down, you can place all sorts of camp fixtures around it.

313251.text: Sufficiently skilled leatherworkers, for example, can place a tent like this one behind me.

313253.text: Every trade has something they can contribute to your camp, even fishermen!

313254.text: Then, all you need to do is have a seat near the fire and soak it all in. After a few minutes of resting, you'll gain various boons that will help you in your travels.

313255.text: If you just sit still and rest for a few more moments, you'll gain a benefit from having rested near the tent I have set up behind me.

313256.text: That's about the gist of it. Once you've gained your boon from resting near the fire, speak with me again.

313453.text: The Windshapers and the High Order are up to something. There are rumors floating around that both groups plan to get the skycutters running again and use them to leave the Skywall. LEAVE SKYWALL? How ridiculous. Where would they even go?

313606.text:
You speak of this place by name! That is a level of respect, or knowledge, that I would not expect these days. Of the few adventurers I have encountered, most refer to the city simply as "Dire Maul".

While I find that name insulting and diminishing of my people's proud and extensive history, I cannot deny that Eldre'Thalas no longer lives up to its historical grandeur. At times I wonder if I do our city a disservice by preserving its namesake so long after it has fallen.

I hope you can excuse the state the temple and its grounds are in. So much has changed over the past few millennia.

313610.text:
I'm inclined to agree. Despite our people coming together to survive the Great Sundering it seems as though the city was nonetheless doomed. How pedantic is it that its fall from grace would come from something so mundane as internal strife?

My loyalty was unquestionable in those days, but in the years since I've come to realize that the rebellion was the moment that we truly lost Prince Tortheldrin. Everything that came after is but a consequence of that wound upon his soul.
 
For my part, I try to avoid dwelling on the past, particularly my role in those events.

Try as I might though... it still haunts me.

313613.text:
Celebrating my own life as I stare toward the mass grave of so many of my kin feels... selfish. Many among my order remain cloistered in Prince Tortheldrin's inner sanctum, I suspect to hide from their own guilt. Seeing the city from this perspective makes it difficult to avoid painful truths.

I still count myself among the Shen'dralar, but these days I am long estranged from the library I once called home.

313648.text: The Nightclaw do not take kindly to reckless intruders. Tread carefully while in Shadowgale, $c.

313982.text:
An outsider approaches me?

I doubt we have much to discuss, unless you are here to aid an old Kolkar.

314601.text: Wait, yes... this crystal! Valennia, is this...

314602.text1: ...a recall crystal! Used to record an important moment, no doubt.

314603.text: This is surely what the turncoat hoped to offer us in exchange for our protection.

314604.text1: The recall crystal is badly damaged, though. The recording is likely to be incomplete, so we must listen carefully.

314605.text: Activate it, Valennia. We need to learn as much as we can about what it contains.

314606.text1: ...do not delay. Muster our forces to march immediately. The pylons are key and...the wards...come down. This is...

314607.text1: ...quickly. With our forces.....will be exposed.....my ritual must not....

314608.text1: I alone am.....this task....the Windlord will.......our voices.....he will come.....we must not fail!

314609.text1: The crystal is too damaged to play any further, I am afraid.

314610.text: Wards... what is this about wards, Valennia?

314611.text1: The anchor pylons keep us suspended in this realm, but they also act as wards! The Shal'nan once spoke of this. They keep us shielded from...

314612.text: ...whatever else is out there in Skywall. Spirits save us... this is her plan. Bring down the wards and let her 'Windlord' in!

Welcome to the Xizzix Asset Recovery Service! If you lost it, we probably found it! 

Check my stock to see if we've recovered anything that you might have carelessly discarded and have since decided you just can't live without.

316033.text: Oh... a $r. What are you doing in our glorious city? These ruins are already crawling with inhuman filth as it is.

316310.text: It is vital that we learn more about what the cult is planning, and with the turncoat dead, the information may have died with him...

316364.text1:
I suppose that is true. I and the rest of my elites used to belong to an order known as the Empyrean Blades. We were the personal guard of our former leader, the Shal'nan. 

In the current, uncertain times we do what we can to help lead the peacekeepers' citizen militia, since we are the closest thing to professional soldiers left on Zephras.

316366.text1:
<Valennia looks away briefly before looking hesitantly back in your direction.>

The Shal'nan was the very best of us. It was he who stood up for our people against madness and oppression in Eldre'Thalas nearly ten thousand years ago. It was the Shal'nan who led us across the uncharted sea to escape the murderous vengeance of our ancient enemies.

It was the Shal'nan who brokered the pact of friendship with the wind spirits that allowed us to ascend to Skywall... and survive.

He was ever the servant leader to his people, even after he abdicated his position of power and retired.

316368.text1:
I might be the only living shen'dorei left amongst our people who had more than a handful of words with him.

I served him as the captain of his Empyrean Blades for nearly nine centuries, right up until... he left us.

Even still, I can't rightly claim that I "knew" him. He was ever a reserved and solitary man. He spent most of his time alone or in communion with the spirits in the spires high above the Shrine of the Four Winds... the place that the cult now calls the 'Shrine of Akir'.

316370.text1:
If I knew that then I suspect that life here on Zephras would be much, much easier. So many of our struggles and conflicts revolve around that very mystery.

I appreciate your curiosity on this matter but I'm afraid that is all I have to say about this for today.

316402.text: I can teach you to swing a blacksmith's hammer, if you are willing to learn.
316402.text1: I can teach you to swing a blacksmith's hammer, if you are willing to learn.

You've earned a degree of trust amongst the Nightclaw, $c. We don't have much to offer you as a reward, but we have managed to scavenge a number of crafting plans from the ruins of Ban'aethal.

The magesmiths of Ban'aethal were widely regarded to be the best artisans in all of the Skyborne Isles. The Nightclaw are naturalists, not crafters, so these records are of little use to us.

Continue to prove yourself to be a valuable ally, and I would make these secrets available to you.

Greetings, $c. Are you in need of arms?

I was trained by Antarion of Ban'aethal, using secrets handed down from the ancient master magesmiths of Kalimdor.

You'll find no finer weapons on Zephras Isle than mine.

324145.text1: All of the skyborne islands became destabilized and began to move apart a few years ago. If that wasn't bad enough, now large pieces of Zephras are beginning to fall away. It's hard to imagine your home falling into the sky, but that is my reality now.

324563.text: For now, spread the word to our people. Be on your guard around Windshapers. We didn't start this fight, but once the cult is dealt with, we will be ready to end it.

324570.text:
Excellent. Go to the font where arcane magic is at its strongest. In the absence of proper Highborne sorcerers walking the world freely once more it is your best bet of having the energy required to cleanse the globe after it has rotted for so long.

I have nearly finished poring over the tome you brought me to finish the blade once you have it. Perhaps there is hope yet that we may witness this masterwork in its intended form.

324693.text:
The Night Dancer is here, untarnished by time! Curious. I suppose you came here seeking aid in restoring the Dawn Waker, then. Very well. For now, our interests align.

My subjects have safeguarded countless pages of knowledge here in the Athenaeum. Perhaps one exists detailing Eluvi'tor's construction that may be of aid. My Lorekeeper may assist with such inquiries--for a mortal such as yourself to pore over the tomes would take many lifetimes. Though he may need convincing; few are as gracious as I am to uninvited interlopers.

Do so, and only then will I consult my own personal archive on what you seek.

324740.text:
Ah, the Arcanum of Binding! I thought it would be the cornerstone of the ritual to bind--never mind. Such knowledge would melt an inferior intellect.

Connecting it to Luminarian's works... yes, it makes sense. How did we not see it before? He did not earn the title of Magesmith merely by his arcane acumen, notable as it was; each of his masterworks involves powerful magic running through the very fibres of the metal. Truly unparalleled craftsmanship!

The power to make what never was, mine...

324742.text:
Silence, mortal. You would do well to know the punishment for interrupting the ruler of this kingdom.

How fortunate--I do possess the passage containing the ritual for the blade, taken from a series of... talks... I had with Luminarian many, many eons ago. The joy of seeing the shift in their eyes as they realize who they contend with. But I digress. It reads:

As night dances on, so must day wake
To rejoin one, its pair must await
So only pure of heart may wield
Blade high or perfect dark must yield

In flames born of air it must be cast
Only then will the spirit bind last

-L

325028.text1: How can I help you, friend?

325816.text: Hello there, $c. I am High Tinker Mekkatorque of the exiles of Gnomeregan.

326162.text:
The Wind Spirits have left us. 

Now, only mindless echoes remain. Be wary, however. These winds are neither kind, nor gentle.

327773.text:
<As you near this saber, it growls menacingly. Its long tail lashes behind it.

It bares its teeth while digging its nails into the soft earth. It would seem its temperament is as stormy as its namesake.

It gently sniffs the air around you, then after a moment, huffs. It seems impressed when you stand your ground.

It seems this saber senses your determination and approves. It will accept you as a worthy rider and champion, should you choose it.>

327778.text1:
<The great cat stretches its long, nimble legs as you approach, making no sound with the motion.

It shakes its head, the armor on its body fitting it snugly so as to also be completely silent with its movements.

It watches you closely, as it flexes its sharp claws. This silent saber eyes you and sniffs the air around you.

In a slight bow it inclines its head toward you, impressed with all you have accomplished. It seems to have found you a worthy champion and rider should you choose it.>

327780.text1:
<As you approach, the saber turns its great head to regard you.

Through the glowing visor of its helm, you can feel its piercing eyes evaluating you. It stands stock-still, the rustling of its fur in the gentle Teldrassil wind being the only movement. It almost seems as if it can sense how you have grown, and all the adventures and trials you have overcome.

After a long moment, it lets out a low growl and inclines its armored head.

It would appear this saber has accepted you as both a stalwart champion and confident rider should you choose it.>

327788.text:
<As you walk up to this ram, it watches you with interest before lowering its head and pointing its horns at you. It gazes steadily at you for a long moment with a challenging snort, then relaxes as recognition flickers in its eyes.

It snorts and shakes the snow from its armored head; its thick ram horns gleam with new nicks and dents from all of the battles it has fought and won since you last met.

This fierce ram seems to sense your determination and approves. It will accept you as its rider and champion.>

327796.text: <The raptor turns to fix you with two vibrant orange eyes.>

327799.text:
<Upon walking up to this kodo, it stands tall and proud next to its kin. Its strong legs cause the earth to shake slightly as it stamps them into the ground. The kodo grunts happily when you near.

It would seem this once timid kodo has found its confidence and is proud of both its strength and fearlessness.
 
It is clear your presence here excites it, and it would be proud to bear you into the grand world as its rider and champion.>

327800.text:
<As you near this kodo, it swivels its powerful neck to regard you, staring you down with keen eyes from under its helmet. It would seem the passage of time has done little to temper its brave and challenging nature.

Long thick scars run the length of its hide and horn. It is clear in your time apart it has become victorious in every battle it has entered against both friend and foe.

As it sizes you up, it relaxes when you don't back down. It seems impressed by your bravery and foes and feats you have overcome in your long journey. It would be proud to bear you as its champion and rider.>

327801.text:
<Nearing this strider, you notice the bird tapping its talons against the moist soil. It stills as you near, perhaps sensing a familiarity about you.

It lets out a soft warble as it regards you, clearly curious about you and the things you have seen since you parted. It seems impressed by all the challenges you have surmounted and the long journey you have been on to get here.

This gentle-natured strider seems fond of you and will happily bear you as its champion and rider.>

327802.text:
<As you approach this strider, the creature lets out a warble and almost seems to bounce with excitement as it recognizes you from before. Even though this strider has matured, it seems it has kept its coloration from the time it was a hatchling, which is unusual.

It stills its agitated movements and fixes you with its golden eyes. After a moment it lets out a gentle warble, clearly impressed at your ability to overcome all that has stood in your path thus far.

After a moment it gently clacks its beak at you, letting out a few more soft warbles. It seems this strider is impressed by your determination and will bear you as its champion and rider.>

327803.text:
<As you near this strider it fixes you with golden eyes, and after a moment it lets out a familiar warble.

This strider has seen more combat since you parted; its legs and beak bear the marks of battle, and its armor shows wear under the polish.

It would seem this adventurous strider approves of you and would delight in traveling to new worlds with you as its champion and rider.>

327804.text: <Even through the visor on its helm, you can feel its gaze as it studies you.>
327804.text1:
<The wolf turns its head to regard you as you draw near. Even through the visor on its helm, you can feel its gaze as it studies you. It sniffs you gently, and after a moment lets out a low but not unfriendly growl in recognition. 

 
It stands up straighter, seemingly to show off the heavy armor adorning its body. The freshly polished metal gleams, even under a coat of Durotar dust kicked up by the hot winds. 

Something within you stirs and you sense that this wolf approves of your bravery and would be proud to bear you as its friend and rider.>

327805.text: <As you approach this wolf it shakes its great head; its armor glints gently against its ashen fur.>

327806.text: <The wolf stands tall and strong, even with the added weight of the armor.>
327806.text1:
<Just as the freshly hewed timbers of a cedar tree fade from red to grey, so too has this timber wolf's fur changed with maturity. Its once boisterous personality is focused, and it stands tall and strong, even with the added weight of the armor. 
 
Its long tail still wags in familiarity as you approach and lets out a knowing whine. Through the glowing enchantment of the helmet's visor, you see its eyes shine with determination; its thirst for adventure is undiminished. 

After a moment it lets out an excited growl. You get the sense that this wolf admires your adventurous spirit and is impressed by all the challenges you have surmounted. It would gladly accept you as a rider and companion.>

329302.text: Hidden within their impregnable stronghold of Ironforge mountain, they rarely ventured beyond the wintry peaks of Dun Morogh.

329309.text: The noble humans of Stormwind are a proud, tenacious race.

329310.text: Though the recent invasion of the demonic Burning Legion decimated their sister kingdom of Lordaeron, the defenders of Stormwind stand vigilant against any who would threaten the sanctity of their lands.

329311.text: Nestled in the foothills of Elwynn Forest, Stormwind city is one of the last bastions of human power in the world.

329312.text: Ruled by the child king Anduin Wrynn, the people of Stormwind remain steadfast in their commitment to the Grand Alliance.

329313.text: Backed by their stalwart allies, the armies of Stormwind have been called away to fight the savage horde on distant battlefields.

329314.text: With the armies gone, the defense of Stormwind now falls to its proud citizens.

329315.text: You must defend the kingdom against the foul mongrels that encroach upon it and hunt down the subversive traitors who seek to destroy it from within.

329730.text: Step back, mortal. I will channel magic so that you may see what I saw...

329731.text: No, Ve'han! Do not do this! You are betraying your oath as a protector of the mountain!

329732.text: Oaths are meaningless if those we serve betray us! Know this before you die, lesser god. Our Pact is strong. We will reclaim what was stolen from us!

329734.text: Yes... I can feel it. The power! I can feel the ancient power returning. I am... invincible!

329735.text: I have never seen magic such as this. He absorbed that demigod's power. Invincible indeed...

329736.text: Even a lesser Wild God contains a font of immense energy. No mortal should have this power.

329737.text: Return to Starblaze and tell him what you've learned, little mortal.

Velician. She was one of the few on this mountain that was a constant voice of reason. One that always sought to find answers when questions arose. I suspect she caught on to the cult long before any of us and went to investigate herself. Which is probably what ultimately led to her demise. 

I... do not know if her spirit will be in the Dream. I do not know what happens to those once their power is taken. I hope she heals and is able to remanifest herself as the rest of us do when we die.
